title: Use a store value as a signal
summary: Store.selectSignal gives an Angular signal for a selected value.
introduction: Store.selectSignal gives an Angular signal for a selected value. Your task: Find the signal read in the template.
learningObjectives: Find the signal read in the template.
Explain the example for use a store value as a signal

blocks.text: Store.selectSignal gives an Angular signal for a selected value. The template reads the signal by calling it.

Use an Angular project with the matching major version of @ngrx/store. Effects and SignalStore examples also need @ngrx/effects or @ngrx/signals. Save linked snippets in the files named by their imports.

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `selectSignal` exposes an NgRx selected value as an Angular signal, read by calling it.

blocks.text: The paragraph follows the selected count from the registered store.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Use count() in the template because this value is a signal. The store and selector must already be configured.
